content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Naperville

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree (high school diploma, associate, or equivalent) and completion of secondary education project management training hours. Notably, no prior work experience is required—making CAPM accessible to career-changers and recent graduates entering project management roles across Naperville's major employers.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of PM Education
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot-camp-style course. This intensive format compresses core project management knowledge—scope, time, cost, quality, communication, and risk—into a focused learning experience you can complete while maintaining your current work schedule.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Register with the Project Management Institute and pay the associated exam fee. PMI will verify your educational prerequisite, then issue authorization to sit for the CAPM exam. Granite PM Academy's team can guide you through the online submission process.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the CAPM Exam
steps_items.text: Study using Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice questions aligned to PMI's CAPM exam domains. Schedule your proctored exam at a Pearson VUE test center and sit for the assessment. Upon passing, you earn the CAPM credential immediately.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: CAPM certification remains valid for three years. To renew, earn professional development units (PDUs) through approved learning activities—courses, volunteering, conference attendance, or publications. Plan your PDU collection early to ensure uninterrupted credential status.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.
